claims.claim: A research team dated a shipwreck off Turkey to 2700–2400 B.C. using pottery vessels.
claims.episode_span: A research team led by Associate Professor Hakan Öniz of Akdeniz University dated the wreck to around 2700–2400 B.C. using pottery vessels recovered from shallow waters near Kekova on the southern Turkish coast.
claims.source_title: World's oldest shipwreck discovered off coast of Turkey
claims.supporting_quote: A shipwreck off the coast of Turkey is the oldest shipwreck in the world, our team of archaeologists believes. There's little left of the ship itself, but based on clues from its cargo—including pottery vessels—a research team I was part of has tentatively dated the wreck to around 2700–2400 B.C.

claims.claim: Methane uptake in certain forest soils rose by an average of 3 percent each year under rising temperatures and declining rainfall.
claims.episode_span: A 24-year monitoring program recorded an average 3 percent annual rise in methane uptake under conditions of rising temperatures and declining rainfall.
claims.source_title: A 24-year study uncovers a surprising climate benefit beneath forests
claims.supporting_quote: Scientists have discovered that some forest soils are becoming surprisingly better at removing methane from the atmosphere as temperatures rise and rainfall declines. A study spanning up to 24 years found methane absorption increasing by an average of 3% annually, challenging previous predictions about climate change's effects on forests.
